library_preparation_preflight.summary: No extra dependency or Docker image needed — azure-core (already a compile dep) provides HttpClient/TokenCredential, which SecretClientBuilder accepts directly for full request mocking, exactly like the existing azure-core-http-jdk-httpclient test.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Do not attempt to reach a real Azure Key Vault or require azure-identity/real credentials. Build the SecretClient/SecretAsyncClient with SecretClientBuilder.httpClient(...) pointed at a local mock server (e.g. com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer, following the pattern in tests/src/com.azure/azure-core-http-jdk-httpclient) and SecretClientBuilder.credential(...) using a minimal in-test TokenCredential implementation that returns a canned com.azure.core.credential.AccessToken (no network call). vaultUrl has no https-only enforcement in the builder itself, so a plain http://localhost:<port> URL works. Craft response bodies matching the Key Vault Secrets REST API JSON schema (id, value, attributes {enabled, created, updated, recoveryLevel}, contentType, tags, kid, managed) so KeyVaultSecret/SecretProperties deserialization is exercised for CRUD-style calls (setSecret, getSecret, updateSecretProperties, listPropertiesOfSecrets, beginDeleteSecret, purgeDeletedSecret, backup/restore). Cover both sync (SecretClient) and async (SecretAsyncClient) surfaces since they use separate implementation classes.
risks: If the library's HttpPipeline default policies (e.g. retry/logging) end up requiring azure-core-http-netty's Reactor Netty client specifically rather than accepting the injected mock HttpClient, an agent may need to fall back to azure-core-http-netty's own SSL/plaintext handling — verify locally with a real nativeTestCompile/test run before assuming the mock-only approach is sufficient.

Long-running operations like beginDeleteSecret/beginRecoverDeletedSecret use polling; the mock server must handle repeated poll requests with status transitions, or tests should avoid exercising the poller to keep the scaffold simple.
